visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) A young woman with brown hair and bangs is seen in a medium shot, wearing a beige t-shirt and white smartwatch. She speaks directly to the camera against a soft-colored background with an abstract poster and a green plant leaf partially visible on the left. The lighting is bright and even. (2) A close-up view shows a pair of pinkish-framed glasses being held and rotated by the woman's hands to show the frame detail and lens thickness. The background is a blurred view of an eyewear store shelf filled with glasses. The hands move precisely. (3) A split-screen visual appears showing a 'Before' and 'After' comparison of the woman's eyes behind different lenses. The top frame shows eyes appearing smaller due to lens distortion, while the bottom frame shows them appearing more natural in size and clarity. (4) A technical graphic appears illustrating the difference between aspherical and spherical lenses. Two grid patterns are shown on a white background; the left grid is perfectly square representing aspherical quality, while the right grid is distorted representing spherical lens limitations. (5) A chart titled 'Lens Thickness' shows cross-sections of lenses at various refractive indices from 1.50 to 1.74. Each section clearly illustrates how the physical edge of the lens becomes significantly thinner as the refractive index value increases for the user. (6) The woman returns to the eye-level medium shot, gesturing with both hands and pointing her finger upwards to emphasize her final advice on selecting smaller frames and specific high-quality brands. She maintains a friendly smile and direct eye contact throughout the clip.

narrative_and_purpose.mainPurpose: The video aims to educate viewers on how to choose eyeglass lenses and frames that do not make the eyes appear smaller. By explaining technical concepts like aspherical lenses and refractive indices, the creator provides a practical guide for people with high myopia to maintain aesthetic eye size.
